newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta to raise limit on issue of treasury bills.
newsitem.headline: Malta to raise limit on issue of treasury bills.

text.p: The Maltese government plans to double the maximum number of treasury bills it can issue, to Lm200 million ($560m).

Finance Minister Lino Spiteri said a motion due to be debated in Parliament on Monday evening was "an indication of the short-term financing requirements of the government within the context of the overall financial position it has inherited".
In January last year parliament set the limit at Lm100 million, which has now been reached.

Treasury bills with maturities of between one month and one year are auctioned every week. Most are taken up by the commercial banks. Parliament in June last year approved amendments making it possible for treasury bills to be held outside Malta.

The one-month yield now stands at 4.999 per cent. The three-month yield stands at 5.005 compared with 4.94 per cent at the end of 1995 and the 12-month yield at 5.36 per cent compared with 5.34 per cent at the end of last year. ($=0.36c)
